answer: No, you should not be taking lisinopril. Your doctor stopped it on September 22, 2025, because of a dry cough, and switched you to losartan 50 mg once a day. Your pharmacy records show no lisinopril prescription since then. The app that still lists it is most likely showing an old copy from a hospital health export made in March 2025, before the change. Please don't restart lisinopril, and don't take it alongside losartan. If you have lisinopril tablets at home, set them aside and ask your pharmacy to close the old prescription. Mention this to Dr. Marsh's office so they can correct the app's list. If you have been taking both, call the office soon, because that combination can raise potassium and strain the kidneys.

knowledge.says: A dry cough is a known side effect of lisinopril, one of the ACE inhibitors, and switching to an angiotensin receptor blocker such as losartan is the usual fix. Taking an ACE inhibitor and an ARB together is generally avoided because it raises the risk of high potassium and kidney injury.
knowledge.guideline: Common clinical practice for ACE-inhibitor cough; ACC/AHA hypertension guidance on avoiding dual RAAS blockade.
